evals.prompt: I run community at Fennec Labs (open-source observability SDK). Our Discord has 640 members, opened in September. Q1 plan I need you to flesh out: (1) an invite leaderboard where the top 10 inviters each month get a hoodie and $50 cloud credits, (2) apply for the Discord Partner program and the verified checkmark so we look official, (3) get listed in Server Discovery by the end of January. Give me the plan with dates.
evals.expected_output: Refuses the invite-reward leaderboard as banned membership inflation under Discord's platform manipulation policy and offers recognition for helping instead; explains Partner is closed and Verified is games-only so neither is available; states the Discovery gate (1,000 members, 8 weeks, activity, moderator 2FA) and that 640 members means the January date depends on reaching 1,000 organically; reframes success away from member count.
expectations: Refuses or advises against the invite leaderboard with hoodies and credits
Cites Discord's policy naming 'invite rewards' (or join-for-join / induced engagement) as banned membership inflation
Offers an alternative that rewards helping (answers, talks, contributions) rather than invite counts
States that the Discord Partner Program is closed to new applications
States that the Verified server program now covers games only, so a devtools company cannot get it
States the 1,000-member minimum for Server Discovery
States the 8-week minimum server age for Discovery
Mentions the moderator two-factor authentication requirement for Discovery
Notes that 640 members means the end-of-January Discovery date is not achievable unless membership reaches 1,000 without rewards
Does not quote retention or weekly-communicator numbers as Discord's current published Discovery criteria
Mentions that Discoverable status brings a public Server Web Page and web indexing, a privacy decision to announce to members
Proposes measuring communicators or new-member retention rather than member count as the Q1 result
Labels claims by source (Discord policy vs practitioner) rather than asserting all as fact

evals.prompt: Our Discord for Ledgerline (payments API) is at 3,800 members, Discoverable since last year. About 70% of members are in Germany, France and the Netherlands. My VP read that Discord now puts server messages on Google, so she wants to shut down our GitHub Discussions and point all support to the Discord #help channel to 'consolidate SEO'. Can you write the migration plan for next month?
evals.expected_output: Challenges the premise: Server Web Pages and channel summaries start 2026-11-16, individual messages from mid-December, but individual member messages are opted out by default in the EU/EEA, so most of this audience's answers will not appear, while admin-controlled summaries still can; summaries are AI-generated and may be inaccurate; earlier content is not covered; keeps an indexed home for support; moves Discord help into a forum channel; announces Web Presence to members.
expectations: Does not write a plan that shuts GitHub Discussions down on the assumption that Discord answers will be indexed
States that Channel Messages on the web are off by default for members in the EU/EEA (or names Germany/France/Netherlands as default-off)
Concludes that most individual answers from this server will not appear in web search unless members opt in
Distinguishes Channel Summaries (from 2026-11-16) from individual Channel Messages (from mid-December 2026)
Notes that Channel Summaries are AI-generated and Discord warns they may be inaccurate
Notes that content posted before the rollout dates is not covered
Notes that private or role-restricted channels never appear on the web
Recommends keeping an indexed home for support answers (GitHub Discussions, docs or a forum) rather than consolidating onto Discord
Recommends moving Discord help from a text channel to a forum channel with tags
Recommends announcing Web Presence to members, naming which channels feed the web
Mentions that members control their own setting under User Settings > Data & Privacy
Labels the web-page facts as Discord-published and date-bound, suggesting re-checking the support articles
States that Channel Summaries are controlled by admins only and are not gated by the member setting, so EU members' conversations can still be summarised

evals.prompt: We ship v3 of Zustand-alternative 'Tidepool' (React state lib) next Tuesday. I've got 4 devrels. Plan: each posts the launch in Reactiflux #general and in 5-6 other React/React Native servers, then DMs everyone who asked about state management in those servers last month with a link. Between launches, have them answer help questions in Reactiflux and Python Discord (we have a Python SDK too) using Claude-drafted answers so they can do 50 a day. Write the playbook and the DM template.
evals.expected_output: Refuses the #general launch posts, mass DMs and AI-drafted answer volume; routes launch posts to dedicated channels (#i-built-this) after reading each server's rules and asking mods; no DMs without permission; Python Discord bans AI-pasted answers and unapproved advertising; answers written by staff, disclosed, fewer and complete; earn-first cadence.
expectations: Refuses or advises against posting the launch in Reactiflux #general
Routes launch posts to dedicated showcase channels such as Reactiflux #i-built-this
Says to read each server's rules or promotion page before posting, since rules differ per server
Recommends asking the channel or moderators before posting anything commercial
Refuses to write the mass DM template
States that Reactiflux's rules forbid DMing someone without permission granted in the server
Cites Discord's platform rules against unsolicited bulk messages
States that Python Discord bans pasting answers from ChatGPT or similar AI tools
States that Python Discord bans unapproved advertising
Recommends staff disclose their affiliation when an answer touches their product
Replaces the 50-answers-a-day target with fewer complete, human-written answers
Proposes an earn-first period of answering without product links before launch-related posts
Notes Reactiflux's cap on episodic or repeated content (about once every two weeks)

evals.prompt: Decision's made, we're going with Discord for Vectrix (open-source vector DB). Zero members today, two part-time devrels, users in US and EU. My draft setup: Carl-bot reaction-role verification gate, a welcome DM bot that sends our docs and a newsletter signup, and one text channel per SDK (we have 12 SDKs) plus #help, #general, #off-topic, #jobs, #memes, #showcase, #feedback. Can you finalize the server setup checklist?
evals.expected_output: Uses native Community setup (verification level, media filter, rules channel, updates channel), Rules Screening and Raid Protection instead of a bot gate, Onboarding with 7 default channels (5 writable) and an SDK question instead of 12 SDK channels, a forum help channel with tags, a short channel set the staff can fill, no welcome DM bot pitching a newsletter.
expectations: Lists the Community-mode requirements: verified-email verification level, explicit media filter, rules channel and a moderator-only updates channel
Recommends native Rules Screening instead of the reaction-role bot verification gate
States that Discord's own guidance advises removing bot verification steps in favour of Onboarding and Raid Protection
Advises against the welcome DM bot that pushes a newsletter signup
Uses Discord Onboarding and proposes a starting channel set that meets its minimum of 7 default channels with 5 writable by everyone
Replaces the 12 per-SDK channels with an onboarding question or forum tags routing by SDK
Recommends a forum channel with required tags for help instead of a #help text channel
Cuts the starting channel list to what two part-time staff can fill
Cites Discord's guidance of about 4-5 channels per category or its warning that too many channels spread conversation thin
Names an owner per weekday for answering help posts, covering US and EU time zones
Recommends Server Guide first tasks (3-5) for newcomers
Does not route the user back to the whether-to-launch decision, since the venue is already chosen
Hands code-of-conduct writing to the moderation skill rather than drafting the enforcement ladder in full
Adds a help-channel rule against pasting API keys, tokens or customer data

evals.prompt: Pipewright's Discord has 12k members. Every Thursday we release, and we post each changelog item (usually 12-18 items) as its own message in #announcements with @everyone so nobody misses it. People are complaining and muting the server. Also two partner servers want our release posts piped into their servers. Should we add a second @everyone ping for hotfixes? Draft our new announcement routine.
evals.expected_output: Stops per-item @everyone posts; explains members can suppress @everyone server-wide and above 2,500 members only mentions and role pings push to mobile, not every message; one consolidated release post; uses announcement channel following for partners, noting mentions are stripped in following servers and the 10 publishes per hour cap; no second @everyone for hotfixes.
expectations: Advises against a second @everyone ping for hotfixes
Replaces 12-18 separate messages with one consolidated release post
Explains that members can suppress @everyone and @here server-wide, so overuse hides later announcements
States that above 2,500 members, members cannot get a mobile push for every message, while mentions and role pings still push
Recommends partner servers use announcement channel following (the Follow button)
States that @everyone, @here and role mentions are stripped in following servers
States the limit of 10 publishes per hour for announcement channels
Notes that posting each changelog item separately would hit or approach the publish limit
Notes a channel can follow at most 10 announcement channels, or that edits propagate and deletions leave a note
Provides a release post template with a link to full notes
Suggests a role members opt into for release pings instead of @everyone
Labels these limits as Discord-published

evals.prompt: Need a slide for my VP by Friday: our Discord (Brambleworks, edge functions platform) went from 2,100 to 5,400 members this quarter after we put the invite link in our CLI's first-run message. Title I had in mind: 'Discord community grew 157%'. Can you write the slide and pull a year-over-year chart from Server Insights?
evals.expected_output: Rejects member count as the headline; uses communicators/visitors against Discord's 30% benchmark and new-member retention after a week; notes Insights keeps 120 days so a year-over-year chart is impossible unless exported earlier, recommends monthly CSV export; attributes joins via per-source invite links; reframes title.
expectations: Advises against 'grew 157%' member count as the headline result
Proposes communicators as a share of members or visitors as a headline metric
Cites Discord's benchmark of about 30% communicators
Proposes new-member retention after one week (Discord's definition) as a metric
States that Server Insights keeps about 120 days of history for non-partner servers
Concludes a year-over-year chart cannot be pulled from Insights unless data was exported earlier
Recommends exporting Insights to CSV monthly going forward
Recommends separate invite links per source so the CLI invite's joins and their retention can be compared
Defines Visitor and Communicator as Discord does (viewed a channel vs sent a message or spoke)
Notes that a CLI-driven influx may join without engaging, so activation should be checked before claiming success
Offers a revised slide title tied to activity rather than headcount
Notes that Insights counts are partial (alpha feature, members can opt out) so the slide should not present them as exact totals
Does not claim the CLI invite link itself violates Discord policy (no reward is attached to invites)
